text:
ops_alert_bot: :rotating_light: detected spike in 5xx/timeouts for hosted inference - eu-west-1. aggregation: 3m window, p95 latency -> 2.4s, 5xx rate 6%

maria: seeing same in SLO dashboard, started a war room. Lots of customer reports about generation timeouts.

devon: initial hunch: routing layer overloaded after autoscaler lag. Kicking off quick checks.

luca: logs show a surge of long tail requests hitting the gateway pods. sample trace IDs: trace-8f3a, trace-8f4b. Pasting a representative stack snippet:
```
2026-03-17T10:12:23Z gateway ERROR request_id=trace-8f3a downstream_timeout after 15s waiting for backend
backend: hosted-inference-euw-01
kvcache_hits=0 queue_depth=48
```

jen: customer-support: two enterprise customers reported ~200 failed requests each, churn risk. They've opened tickets.

eli: tried reproducing with curl, small payloads succeed, large-batch (seqlen 1024) reproduces higher timeout rate. Repro steps below:
```bash
for i in {1..50}; do 
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    -d '{"model":"rw-7b", "input":"'$(printf 'x%.0s' {1..500})'"}' &
done
```
Most failures when 10+ concurrent long requests.

maria: mitigation idea: temporary throttle per-tenant at gateway, and enable fallback to smaller model variant. Can we flip on per-tenant concurrency caps?

luca: we have a runtime flag for per-tenant qps but not concurrency. Quick win: apply a circuit breaker at gateway to 8 concurrent per-connection and short-circuit to rw-3b as fallback.

devon: rolling out config change to ingress to limit concurrent connections to 8 for eu-west-1 (canary on 2 pods first).

ops_alert_bot: deploy started by devon at 10:20 UTC. Canary on pod gw-102 and gw-103.

sam: watching metrics: after canary rollout, 5xx rate dropped from 6% -> 1.2% on those pods. Latency p95 also improved on canary.

jen: messaging customers: will notify affected customers of temporary fallback and share ETA for rollback to normal when safe. Draft msg ready.

eli: rollout to all gateway pods completed at 10:42 UTC. Full fleet 5xx rate dropped to 0.9%.

maria: good. capture timeline: alert 10:10 -> canary 10:20 -> full rollout 10:42 -> stabilization 10:50.

luca: root cause hypothesis: a small set of high-cost long-seqlen requests saturated backend request queues; autoscaler reacted too slowly because of metric smoothing and warmup. KV cache miss amplification exacerbated (lots of unique prefixes).

devon: immediate action items: 1) keep the concurrency caps for 24h, 2) add a per-tenant long-request detector to route to lower-cost variants, 3) adjust autoscaler to react faster to queue depth signals.

jen: comms action: send notice to customers affected and update status page with summary. I'll own customer comms.

eli: engineering follow-ups: add pagination/size limits guidance to API docs, add sample code for client-side retry/backoff, and recommend smaller default model for high fanout.

maria: postmortem tasks (assignments):
- luca: instrument queue-depth metric per-model and per-tenant (due 2026-04-02)
- devon: modify autoscaler to use queue depth and shorten scaling cooldown (due 2026-04-09)
- eli: implement automatic fallback routing for long-seqlen requests (due 2026-04-05)
- jen: customer comms and triage notes (due 2026-03-19)
- sam: runbook update with concurrency cap playbook and rollback steps (due 2026-03-22)

luca: also recommend post-incident load test that mimics high-seqlen fanout (I can schedule with qa).

devon: will also add an emergency runbook hook to temporarily raise dedicated capacity if thresholds crossed.

maria: recording minutes and creating postmortem doc. Please add any missing details here. Thanks everyone for fast triage. :thumbsup:

ops_alert_bot: incident resolved: stabilization confirmed 10:50 UTC. Closing war room channel at 11:00 UTC.
